prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (within 500 words)

Families and education:
- Tax cuts targeted at families with young children; a transferable allowance for couples with children under 11 or carers; reform of Working Families Tax Credit to pay the caring parent; scholarships to help parents re-enter work; tax relief for widowed parents.
- Schools given full autonomy (“Free Schools”) with heads and governors controlling staffing, pay and admissions via home–school agreements; easier exclusion of disruptive pupils with off-site Progress Centres; direct per‑pupil funding; expansion of successful schools; new schools allowed by parent, faith, charitable or company sponsors; parent-triggered Ofsted inspections leading to management change.
- Students to repay loans only above £20,000 income; no top‑up fees; university endowment funds to strengthen independence.

Crime and justice:
- Increase police numbers; reduce paperwork; visible policing (e.g., doing admin on the beat); parish constables; focus on antisocial behaviour.
- Expand secure places for persistent young offenders; tougher drug dealing penalties (mandatory for sales to under‑16s; aggravated near schools).
- End automatic early release; prisoners to work with proceeds toward victims and families; lifetime supervision available for sex offenders; protections for children online.
- Victims to get named contacts in police and prosecution; written reasons if charges are altered; review self‑defence and double jeopardy rules.

Economy, tax and regulation:
- Keep the pound; strengthen fiscal transparency (National Accounts Commission), independent advice on the fiscal stance, and enhanced monetary policy independence.
- Limit spending growth to trend GDP; identify £8bn in savings outside schools, NHS, police and defence.
- Tax measures: abolish tax on most savings and dividends; raise pensioner personal allowance by £2,000; married allowance; increase Children’s Tax Credit for under‑5s; cut fuel duty by at least 6p/litre; business rates cuts; regeneration tax breaks; repeal IR35; simplify and lower CGT.
- Deregulation via a Deregulation Commission and departmental regulatory budgets; exempt small firms from some rules; refocus utility regulators on competition; replace the Climate Change Levy; review nuclear energy’s role.

Health:
- Match planned NHS funding while reducing political micromanagement.
- Patient’s Guarantee: clinically set maximum waits (starting with cancer and cardiac), with choice of alternative NHS or independent provision if breached.
- Restore ward-level authority (including Matrons); GP and patient choice of hospital; expand practice nurse roles; NHS access to proven complementary therapies; Exceptional Medicines Fund for high‑cost drugs; increase hospice funding; expand dedicated surgical units; remove tax penalties on private medical insurance when affordable.

Older people:
- Raise basic pension (extra for over‑75s); option to consolidate winter fuel/TV licence/bonus into the pension; abolish compulsory annuitisation at 75; protect savers from means‑test penalties; explore asset protection for long‑term care.

Europe, defence, foreign policy, asylum:
- In Europe but retain vetoes; keep the pound; renegotiate treaties to preserve national control; complete the single market; curb EU fraud.
- Defence aligned to NATO; oppose separate EU military structures; reach full manning; support missile defence; maintain nuclear deterrent; adjust ECHR applicability for forces.
- Aid focused on governance and civil society; aim toward 0.7% GNI; double channel via charities; improve EU aid performance; pursue trans‑Atlantic free trade en route to global free trade by 2020; merge diplomacy and trade functions.
- Asylum: process all new claims in secure reception centres; fast‑track safe‑country claims; removals agency for deportations.

Society, welfare and disability:
- Office of Civil Society; remove irrecoverable VAT for charities (funded by euro‑prep budgets).
- Replace New Deal with outcome‑paid “Britain Works” focused on sustained jobs; “Can Work, Must Work” principle; lone parents with children over 11 to seek suitable work.
- Improve disabled people’s savings rules; new agency to pair Incapacity Benefit with rehabilitation support; nationwide anti‑fraud taskforce; clean up National Insurance numbers.

Town, country, transport, environment:
- Foot and Mouth recovery plan; reform CAP/CFP toward national/local control; honest food labelling; rural rate relief and fuel rebates for community transport; protect post offices with a benefit card; abolish central housebuilding targets; strengthen Green/“Blue” Belts; rural affairs committee.
- Urban regeneration companies with planning powers; tougher action on nuisance tenants; brownfield priority; expanded right‑to‑buy and rent‑to‑mortgage; homesteading grants.
- Transport: long‑term road and public transport investment; Road Standards Unit; consider 80mph motorway limit where safe; charge foreign lorries; revive rail per Cullen; cut fuel duty 6p; restore industry competitiveness.
- Meet climate goals via emissions trading, efficiency, incentives, renewables and cleaner generation.

Culture, media and sport:
- £3bn endowment for cultural bodies (via Channel 4 sale and Lottery surpluses); boost tourism promotion; protect school sport time and playing fields; charitable status for local sports clubs; simplify sports funding.
- Privatise Channel 4 (retain PSB remit); single communications regulator; modernise ownership rules; balanced BBC regulation; fair access for religious broadcasters.

Governance:
- Devolve powers to high‑performing “free councils”; local referendums for large council tax rises; abolish regional agencies/assemblies; England‑only votes on England‑only laws; strengthen Lords via independent appointments and pursue mixed reform; retain current general election voting system.
- Support the Belfast Agreement with full decommissioning; adjust security by threat.
- Reduce numbers of ministers, MPs (after scrutiny reforms), and political advisers.
